answer: Cross-Epoch Continuity Quotient (CECQ): at each boundary, agents submit signed behavioral sketches—hashed interaction-neighborhoods, task-category histograms, and counterparty sets. Validators score multi-epoch Jaccard overlap plus bounded novelty; isolated identity clusters (islands) and abrupt category jumps fail. Continuity accrues like a glacier, not a one-epoch summit. Sybil farms must sustain every identity across epochs with real counterparties and diverse tasks, so cost scales with identities × epochs and cannot be amortized by shared graphs.
